caption: New Jersey v. Dow Chemical Co.
citation_line: New Jersey v. Dow Chemical Co., No. 3:23-cv-02449; aff’d, No. 24-1753 (3d Cir. June 11, 2025)
headnote_district_ruling: Judge Kirsch remanded New Jersey’s environmental suit over 1,4-dioxane to state court, rejecting Dow’s contention that federal specifications made it a person “acting under” a federal officer for purposes of 28 U.S.C. § 1442(a)(1).
qualification_rationale: The precedential ruling clarifies the boundary of federal-officer removal for a private manufacturer that helped develop and sold products meeting government specifications—a recurring issue in mass-tort and environmental litigation.
appellate_posture_note: The Third Circuit affirmed in a precedential opinion, holding that the record did not establish the required government-assistance or delegation relationship.
